items.definition: On-time delivery is the share of deliveries (or shipments, or order lines) that happened on or before the committed date, within any agreed tolerance.
items.definition_ar: نسبة التسليم في الموعد هي نسبة عمليات التسليم (أو الشحنات أو بنود الطلبات) التي تمت في الموعد الملتزم به أو قبله ضمن أي هامش متفق عليه.
items.explanation: The result depends entirely on which date is the commitment (requested, promised or carrier schedule), the unit counted and the tolerance. Two teams reporting 'OTD' can differ by 20 points without either being wrong; state the definition with every figure.

kpi.formula: on-time units ÷ units delivered in the period × 100
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio over the period (not an average of daily percentages)
kpi.period: usually weekly or monthly, by delivery date
exclusions: units not yet delivered (report them separately as open/overdue)
units with no committed date (report the count)
limitations: Early deliveries count as on time unless the definition says otherwise.
Ignores how late the late ones were — pair with average days late.

items.example: 40 shipments delivered in March, 34 on or before the promised date: OTD = 34 ÷ 40 = 85%.

items.definition: OTIF is the share of orders (or order lines) delivered both on time and in full — the complete quantity of the right items — in one measure.
items.definition_ar: مؤشر OTIF هو نسبة الطلبات (أو بنودها) التي سُلمت في الموعد وبالكامل (الكمية الكاملة من الأصناف الصحيحة) معًا.
items.explanation: OTIF is always at or below the lower of on-time and in-full alone, because an order must pass both. Counting by line instead of by order raises the figure; say which.

kpi.formula: orders delivered on time AND in full ÷ orders due in the period × 100
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio over the period
kpi.period: weekly or monthly, by committed date
exclusions: orders cancelled by the customer
orders with no committed date (count them separately)
limitations: Definitions of 'in full' vary (units, value, lines); fix it before comparing.
A partial delivery completed later still fails OTIF for the order.

items.example: 100 orders due: 90 on time, 92 in full, 85 both: OTIF = 85%.

items.definition: SLA compliance is the share of transactions that met the service level agreed in a contract — a turnaround time, a cut-off, an accuracy target.
items.definition_ar: الالتزام باتفاقية مستوى الخدمة هو نسبة العمليات التي حققت مستوى الخدمة المتفق عليه في العقد (زمن إنجاز، موعد نهائي، دقة).

kpi.formula: transactions meeting the SLA target ÷ transactions in scope × 100
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio per SLA measure
exclusions: the contract's own exclusions (force majeure, customer-caused delays)
limitations: Only as good as the start and end events' timestamps.
An SLA met on average can still fail important individual cases.

items.definition: Transit time as a KPI is the elapsed time between two named events (e.g. ATD to ATA, port to port), summarised over shipments on a lane.
items.definition_ar: زمن العبور كمؤشر هو المدة المنقضية بين حدثين محددين (مثل ATD إلى ATA) ملخصة لشحنات مسار معين.

kpi.formula: per shipment: end event time − start event time; report median and 90th percentile per lane and mode
kpi.aggregation: median and percentile per lane/mode — not a single average across lanes
exclusions: shipments missing either event (count them)
different service levels mixed together
limitations: Averages hide unreliability; the spread matters as much as the middle.
Mixing lanes makes carriers incomparable.

items.definition: Order lead time is the elapsed time from placing a purchase order to the goods being received and available.
items.definition_ar: زمن توريد الطلب هو المدة من إصدار أمر الشراء حتى استلام البضاعة وإتاحتها.

kpi.formula: receipt date − PO date, per order; report median and spread by supplier and mode
kpi.aggregation: median and percentiles per supplier/mode
exclusions: orders still open (track their age instead)
limitations: Includes supplier, transport and clearance time together; break it down to act on it.

items.definition: Backlog is the amount of open work at a point in time: shipments not yet cleared, orders not yet delivered, cases not yet closed.
items.definition_ar: المتراكم هو حجم الأعمال المفتوحة في لحظة معينة: شحنات لم تُخلص، طلبات لم تُسلم، حالات لم تُغلق.

kpi.formula: count of items open at the snapshot time
kpi.aggregation: point-in-time snapshot (do not add snapshots together)
exclusions: cancelled items
limitations: A flat backlog can hide ageing items; read it with ageing.

items.definition: Ageing measures how long open items have been open, usually in buckets (0–7, 8–30, 31–60, over 60 days) or against their own due date.
items.definition_ar: التقادم يقيس منذ متى الأعمال المفتوحة مفتوحة، عادة في شرائح (0-7، 8-30، 31-60، أكثر من 60 يومًا) أو مقارنة بتاريخ استحقاقها.

kpi.formula: per open item: snapshot date − start date (or − due date for days past due); count per bucket
kpi.aggregation: distribution at a snapshot; also the oldest items by name
exclusions: closed items
limitations: Bucket edges are a business choice; keep them fixed to compare over time.

items.definition: Throughput is the number of units completed per period: shipments cleared per week, containers moved per day, lines picked per hour.
items.definition_ar: الإنتاجية هي عدد الوحدات المنجزة لكل فترة: شحنات مخلصة أسبوعيًا، حاويات يوميًا، بنود مجهزة في الساعة.

kpi.formula: units completed in the period ÷ length of the period
kpi.aggregation: sum over the period
exclusions: reopened or reversed units counted twice
limitations: High throughput with rising backlog means demand exceeds capacity.

items.definition: The exception rate is the share of shipments (or transactions) that had at least one exception in the period.
items.definition_ar: نسبة الاستثناءات هي نسبة الشحنات أو العمليات التي حدث فيها استثناء واحد على الأقل خلال الفترة.

kpi.formula: units with ≥1 exception ÷ units handled × 100
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio; also by exception type
exclusions: exceptions logged in error
limitations: Depends on how consistently exceptions are logged; under-reporting looks like good performance.

synonyms: how do we measure carrier performance
items.definition: A carrier scorecard combines measures per carrier — on-time performance, transit time and its spread, tracking data quality, claims, invoice accuracy, responsiveness — over the same lanes and period.
items.definition_ar: بطاقة أداء الناقل تجمع مقاييس لكل ناقل (الالتزام بالمواعيد، زمن العبور وتباينه، جودة بيانات التتبع، المطالبات، دقة الفواتير، الاستجابة) على نفس المسارات والفترة.

kpi.formula: each measure per carrier on comparable lanes; optional weighted score = Σ(weight × normalised measure)
kpi.aggregation: per carrier per lane/mode; minimum sample size per cell
exclusions: cells with too few shipments to judge (show them as not enough data)
limitations: Weights are a business choice.
Different lane mixes make raw averages unfair.

synonyms: freight cost as percent of sales
items.definition: Freight cost is the total paid for transport in a period, often shown per unit (per shipment, kg, TEU) or as a share of the goods' value.
items.definition_ar: تكلفة الشحن إجمالي ما دُفع للنقل خلال فترة، وغالبًا تُعرض لكل وحدة (شحنة، كجم، حاوية) أو كنسبة من قيمة البضاعة.

kpi.formula: Σ freight invoices in the period (base + surcharges + accessorials); ratio form: freight cost ÷ goods value × 100
kpi.aggregation: sum; ratios over the same scope
kpi.period: monthly, by invoice or by shipment date (state which)
exclusions: duties and taxes (they are not freight)
limitations: Accruals vs invoices differ in timing.
Currency conversion date changes the total.

items.definition: Cost per shipment is total logistics (or freight) cost divided by the number of shipments in the same scope and period.
items.definition_ar: التكلفة لكل شحنة هي إجمالي تكلفة اللوجستيات أو الشحن مقسومًا على عدد الشحنات في نفس النطاق والفترة.

kpi.formula: total cost ÷ number of shipments
kpi.aggregation: ratio of totals (not an average of per-shipment ratios)
exclusions: shipments with no cost recorded (or cost with no shipment)
limitations: Shipment size varies; per kg or per TEU is often fairer.

items.example: USD 52,000 freight for 130 shipments = USD 400 per shipment.

items.definition: Accessorial charges are charges beyond the base freight for extra services or events: waiting time, storage, demurrage, detention, re-delivery, special equipment, amendments.
items.definition_ar: الرسوم الإضافية الطارئة هي رسوم تتجاوز أجرة الشحن الأساسية مقابل خدمات أو أحداث إضافية: الانتظار، التخزين، الديمراج، الاحتجاز، إعادة التسليم، معدات خاصة، تعديلات.

kpi.formula: accessorial amount ÷ total freight amount × 100 (and amount by type)
kpi.aggregation: sum by type and by cause
exclusions: contracted surcharges that are part of the agreed rate
limitations: Many accessorials are avoidable; the cause matters more than the total.

items.definition: Cost variance is the difference between what a shipment cost and what was expected (quote, contract rate or budget), in amount and percent.
items.definition_ar: انحراف التكلفة هو الفرق بين التكلفة الفعلية للشحنة والمتوقعة (عرض سعر أو سعر تعاقد أو موازنة)، بالقيمة والنسبة.

kpi.formula: variance = actual − expected; variance % = (actual − expected) ÷ expected × 100
kpi.aggregation: sum of amounts; percent on the summed amounts
exclusions: shipments with no expected cost
limitations: A positive variance is overspend by this sign convention; say the sign convention.

items.definition: ETA accuracy measures how close the forecast arrival was to the actual arrival — for example the share of shipments whose ETA, as known N days before arrival, was within ±1 day of the ATA.
items.definition_ar: دقة الـ ETA تقيس قرب موعد الوصول المتوقع من الفعلي، مثل نسبة الشحنات التي كان الـ ETA المعروف قبل N أيام من الوصول ضمن ±يوم من الـ ATA.

kpi.formula: per shipment: |ATA − ETA as of a fixed horizon|; KPI = share within tolerance; also mean absolute error
kpi.aggregation: over shipments with both an ETA snapshot and an ATA
exclusions: shipments with no ETA at the chosen horizon
limitations: Needs ETA history: the latest ETA alone is almost always close to the ATA and proves nothing.

items.definition: Dwell time is how long cargo stays at a node — usually a container from discharge to gate-out at the destination terminal.
items.definition_ar: زمن المكوث هو المدة التي تبقاها البضاعة في نقطة ما، وعادة الحاوية من التفريغ حتى الخروج من بوابة محطة الوجهة.

kpi.formula: gate-out time − discharge time, per container; median and share over free time
kpi.aggregation: median and percentile per terminal
exclusions: transshipment containers (they leave by sea)
limitations: Long dwell is usually clearance or pickup delay, not the terminal's fault.

items.definition: Clearance cycle time is the elapsed time from the start of clearance (arrival or document submission) to customs release.
items.definition_ar: زمن التخليص هو المدة من بداية التخليص (الوصول أو تقديم المستندات) حتى الإفراج الجمركي.

kpi.formula: release date − clearance start date, per shipment; median and percentiles by BU and mode
kpi.aggregation: median and percentiles per BU/mode/agent
exclusions: shipments not yet released (track their age)
limitations: The start event must be the same for all (arrival vs submission changes the result).

sources.note: The WTO TFA encourages publishing average release times; the formula here is ATLAS's own summary.

items.definition: In this platform a shipment is past due when its clearance is still open (current step is not Completed) and the eHub export's Performance figure — days past the current step's expected completion date — is above zero. The share is past-due shipments ÷ open shipments.
items.definition_ar: في هذه المنصة تُعتبر الشحنة متأخرة إذا كان تخليصها مفتوحًا (الخطوة الحالية ليست Completed) وكان رقم Performance في تصدير eHub (أيام التأخر عن تاريخ الإنجاز المتوقع للخطوة الحالية) أكبر من صفر. والنسبة = الشحنات المتأخرة ÷ الشحنات المفتوحة.
items.explanation: The days come from eHub's own Performance column, as of the export's date; ATLAS does not recompute them. A row whose expected completion date is missing or invalid is counted as data needing attention, not as past due.

kpi.formula: count(open AND Performance > 0) ÷ count(open) × 100
kpi.aggregation: snapshot of the loaded export, by BU, step, agent or forwarder
kpi.period: as of the export's latest date
exclusions: completed shipments
open rows with no valid expected completion date (reported as data quality)
limitations: Only as current as the last uploaded export.
Measures the current step only, not the whole clearance.

items.definition: The Clearance page counts a shipment as on time from eHub's own 'On Time' column (Yes/No). ATLAS does not compute it; a value other than Yes or No is counted as not on time and reported as unclear.
items.definition_ar: تحسب صفحة التخليص الشحنة في الموعد من عمود 'On Time' في eHub (نعم/لا)، ولا تحسبه ATLAS بنفسها؛ وأي قيمة غير نعم أو لا تُحسب غير في الموعد ويُبلغ عنها كقيمة غير واضحة.

kpi.formula: count(On Time = Yes) ÷ count(rows in the selection) × 100
kpi.aggregation: over the rows on screen
exclusions: none; unclear values count as not on time and are reported
limitations: eHub's definition of on time is eHub's; ATLAS reports it, it does not redefine it.

items.definition: Fill rate is the share of demand supplied from stock at the first attempt, measured by units, lines or orders.
items.explanation: Unit fill rate is usually higher than order fill rate, because an order fails if any one line is short. Say which one is reported.

kpi.formula: quantity supplied at first attempt ÷ quantity ordered × 100 (units, lines or orders — state which)
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio over the period
exclusions: orders cancelled by the customer
limitations: Units, lines and orders give different figures; compare like with like.
Supply from a later backorder does not count as filled at first attempt.

items.definition: Inventory turnover is how many times average inventory is used (sold or consumed) in a period: cost of goods sold ÷ average inventory value.
items.explanation: Days of inventory on hand is its inverse in days: average inventory ÷ COGS × days in the period. Low turnover on spare parts can be right for slow critical items; compare like with like.

kpi.formula: cost of goods sold in the period ÷ average inventory value in the period
kpi.aggregation: ratio over the period
exclusions: consignment stock not owned
limitations: Value-based: price changes move it without any physical change.
A two-point average (opening + closing ÷ 2) hides swings within the period.

items.definition: Forecast accuracy measures how close forecasts were to actual demand; a common error measure is the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE): the average of |actual − forecast| ÷ actual.
items.explanation: MAPE cannot be computed for a period with zero actual demand, and it penalises over- and under-forecasting differently in practice. For intermittent spare-parts demand, weighted measures are often used instead.

kpi.formula: mean over periods of |actual − forecast| ÷ actual × 100; accuracy is often reported as 100 − MAPE
kpi.aggregation: mean over periods (and items)
exclusions: periods with zero actual demand (MAPE is undefined there)
limitations: Undefined when actual demand is zero; misleading for intermittent demand.
Averaging across items lets small items dominate unless weighted.

items.definition: The perfect order rate is the share of orders delivered on time, in full, undamaged and with correct documentation and invoice.
items.explanation: It is stricter than OTIF because it adds condition and paperwork. Which conditions count must be fixed in advance.

kpi.formula: orders meeting every agreed condition ÷ total orders × 100
kpi.aggregation: count-based ratio over the period
exclusions: orders cancelled by the customer
limitations: Organisations define the conditions differently; compare only with the same definition.
